speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a significant medical history along with gait and limb ataxia; to begin our evaluation, have you noticed any other neurological symptoms such as weakness, numbness, or vision changes? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Vitamin_B12_level, Thyroid_Stimulating_Hormone.

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial laboratory results are normal. Given your history of gait and limb ataxia, have you noticed any progressive loss of vibration or position sense in your feet and legs? REQUEST TEST: Sensory_Evoked_Potentials.

speaker: Doctor
text: The sensory evoked potentials are also normal, which makes a primary sensory neuropathy less likely. Given your gait and limb ataxia, have you experienced any tremors, intention tremors, or difficulties with coordination like buttoning your shirt? REQUEST TEST: Cerebrospinal_Fluid_Analysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The cerebrospinal fluid analysis has returned normal results, which helps rule out infectious or inflammatory causes like MS or neurosyphilis. Given your significant medical history and persistent ataxia with normal metabolic and sensory testing, do you have a known history of head trauma, substance abuse, or chronic alcohol use? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient describes a recent onset of gait instability and clumsiness affecting the right side more than the left. Before we review your MRI, have you noticed any changes in your speech pattern, such as slurring or difficulty finding words?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

The patient's history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, combined with new-onset asymmetric limb ataxia and gait disturbance, is highly suspicious for PML. I am reviewing the MRI images now to confirm white matter lesions consistent with this diagnosis.
